numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For integer array inputs (int16, int32), signal.resample_poly returns an array consisting only of zeroes; the filter coefficients are cast to the integer dtype of x, truncating them to zero.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: resample_poly should return a non-zero resampled signal for integer inputs, matching the float32/float64 results (e.g. for input [0,1,2,3,2,1,0] with up=2, down=1, padtype='smooth', the float64 output begins approximately [2.98889238e-17, 4.68095127e-01, 1.00051747e+00, 1.44709367e+00, ...]).
trigger_conditions: input x has integer dtype such as int16 or int32
resample_poly called with up=2, down=1, padtype='smooth'
the FIR filter h is cast with .astype(x.dtype), so integer dtype truncates the filter coefficients to zero

input_output_examples.input: numpy.fromiter([0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 0], dtype='int16'), signal.resample_poly(example_input, up=2, down=1, padtype='smooth')
numpy.fromiter([0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 0], dtype='int32'), signal.resample_poly(example_input, up=2, down=1, padtype='smooth')

oracle_clues: Issue reports float32/float64 output of the same input as the reference, which should match integer output
Fix in PR#21686 (gh-15620) builds the filter as float for non-floating inputs instead of casting to x.dtype; the testsuite is referenced but no tolerance is given

numerical_characteristics.dtype: int16, int32 (integer inputs produce all-zero output); float32 and float64 produce nonzero results
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Integer-input output is exactly zero everywhere; float32 and float64 reference outputs have peak about 3.0 and near-zero values around 2.99e-17 at the endpoints
category_specific_evidence: Reproducer input [0,1,2,3,2,1,0] with up=2, down=1, padtype='smooth' gives all zeros for int16 and int32 dtypes, e.g. 'dtype = int16, result = [0. 0. 0. ... 0.]' with 14 entries

Root cause in the passages: the FIR filter h was built with firwin(...).astype(x.dtype), which truncates the filter coefficients to zero when x is an integer dtype; the fix applies the astype only when np.issubdtype(x.dtype, np.floating)
Regression test test_gh_15620 parametrized over np.int32 and np.float32 asserts np.count_nonzero(actual) > 0 for the same input
The fix (PR#21686) enforces dtype preservation for floating inputs only, not integer inputs; integer inputs use the unconverted float filter
Reporter notes the regression: output is an obviously wrong all-zero array; workaround is converting input to float first
reproduction_risks: The passages do not state an expected value or formula for the integer case; the correct output is only implied by the float results, so a comparison target must be derived from float64 behaviour
Discussion of complex input acceptance is unresolved, so complex dtypes should not be assumed supported
The float32 output exhibits a non-zero endpoint value of about -0.127 at the last sample; exact comparison with float64 would need a tolerance that the passages do not specify
